newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Sihanouk rejects mediating in Cambodian tension.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk rejects mediating in Cambodian tension.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk has rejected calls to try to resolve political tensions between the country's two feuding prime ministers by organising round-table talks, a statement on Saturday said.

The king's statement from Beijing, where he is recovering from eye surgery, said by doing so he would be accused of trying to gain power and said it was up to co-premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen and their parties to sort out their differences.

Sihanouk said compatriots in Cambodia and overseas had urged him to call Ranariddh and Hun Sen to a meeting in the hope of leading the country out of the political turmoil that has dogged it since March.
"I would like our nation to forgive me because I cannot meet the request," the king wrote.
"These kinds of things cannot offer the prospect of success from any round table meeting under my chairmanship," wrote the king in the statement released by the royal palace.

"It is not Norodom Sihanouk who has the ability to end the huge crisis," he wrote. He said a solution must be reached in "the minds of Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen and in the minds of other leaders...of FUNCINPEC and the Cambodian People's Party."
Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC and the formerly communist Cambodian People's Party of Hun Sen formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993.
Already poor relations have worsened dramatically since a deadly March 30 grenade attack on an opposition rally led by FUNCINPEC ally Sam Rainsy.
Ranariddh is particularly bitter at Hun Sen's support for a challenge to the prince's leadership of FUNCINPEC, announced by royalist dissidents in mid-April.
The two premiers have since vowed not to resort to violence after rumours of a coup bid swept the capital, but they continue sniping at one another.

"If I dare to intervene in this thing, there are some senior officials who will condemn me by charging that I want to take power from them in violation of the Cambodian constitution," Sihanouk wrote. The constitution says the king reigns but does not rule.
